categories.main_business_segments: CEC operates two main business segments: the Digital Industry Business, which provides ICT services and products to support efficiency, quality, and product development mainly for manufacturing clients; and the Service Integration Business, which offers comprehensive ICT lifecycle support including cloud and security services for corporate and organizational clients.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: CEC's core technologies include system development, cloud integration, cybersecurity, IoT, and digital transformation (DX) solutions. The company emphasizes proprietary platforms such as Connected CI®, SimuField®, LogiPull®, SmartSESAME®, at Claps®, Convergent®, and Re@nove®, and employs advanced project management, quality assurance, and both in-house and outsourced development methodologies.
categories.primary_customers_markets: CEC primarily serves manufacturing companies (especially automotive and logistics), as well as a broad range of enterprises and public sector organizations seeking digital transformation, system integration, and ICT infrastructure solutions. The company’s end markets include manufacturing, automotive, logistics, and public sector clients.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are predominantly in Japan, with major offices and data centers across the country, and a small presence in China (Shanghai) for offshore development. Over 90% of revenue and assets are concentrated in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: CEC operates as a midstream and downstream player in the ICT value chain, providing system integration, software development, and managed ICT services directly to end users and enterprises, while also acting as a solution provider and systems integrator.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: CEC’s strategic focus is on strengthening its core business while accelerating business model transformation, expanding business domains, and creating new businesses. Key R&D themes include smart factories, connected mobility, cloud and security services, and proprietary platform development, with a strong emphasis on DX, sustainability, and human capital development.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through project-based system development, ICT service contracts, cloud and security service subscriptions, maintenance, and product sales. Revenue recognition is based on both progress-based and point-in-time delivery, depending on contract type.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: CEC competes with major Japanese system integrators and ICT service providers such as Fujitsu, NTT Data, and NEC, as well as specialized DX and cloud solution vendors. The company positions itself as a mid-sized, highly trusted, and essential partner with strong manufacturing and enterprise sector expertise.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended January 2025, CEC reported consolidated sales of 56.2 billion yen and net income of 4.0 billion yen, with approximately 2,270 employees. The company has demonstrated steady revenue and profit growth over recent years, with a long-term target of 100 billion yen in sales by FY2031 and a medium-term target of 72 billion yen by FY2028.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CEC differentiates itself through deep industry knowledge, especially in manufacturing and logistics, proprietary digital platforms, comprehensive ICT lifecycle support, and a strong focus on quality, security, and sustainability. The company emphasizes its role as an 'essential company' for clients’ digital transformation and business innovation.
